The data shared must be the researcher's own scholarly work that they have the right to distribute under the chosen license and not contain sensitive information.

items.name: Flanders Research Information Space
items.description: FRIS (Flanders Research Information Space) is a regional research information portal that aggregates and provides up-to-date metadata on publicly funded research in Flanders, including researchers, projects, publications and other outputs. It aims to increase the visibility of Flemish research, support networking and interdisciplinary collaboration, and serve as a resource for reporting, analysis and policymaking.

items.name: FlyGlycoDB
items.description: The glycobiology of Drosophila has been extensively studied in recent years, and much information has accumulated regarding glycan-related genes and proteins in Drosophila. As a database for glycan-related genes in Drosophila, FlyGlycoDB provides specific access to this information.

items.name: Food Database
items.description: The Food Database (FOODB) is a comprehensive resource on food constituents, chemistry, and biology. It is a freely accessible electronic database that provides detailed information about the chemical constituents found in food, designed for applications in nutrition, food science, dietary planning, and general education. FOODB contains extensive data on food compounds, including their chemical properties, biological activities, dietary sources, and health effects.

items.name: FOUNDRY-ML
items.description: Foundry-ML is an open-source platform that provides curated, machine-learning-ready datasets for materials science and chemistry research. It offers structured datasets with standardized metadata, including tabular data, images, and hierarchical scientific data formats. The platform focuses on scientific data such as materials properties, chemical structures, experimental measurements, and simulation results to support reproducible ML workflows in scientific discovery.

items.name: Framework for Open and Reproducible Research Training - Curated Resources
items.description: FORRT is a Framework for Open and Reproducible Research Training which is advancing research transparency, reproducibility, rigor, and ethics through pedagogical reform and meta-scientific research. FORRT provides a pedagogical infrastructure and open educational resources designed to support the teaching and mentoring of open and reproducible science. This record is for the curated resources database crowdsourced by the FORRT community and hosted at https://forrt.org/resources/
subjects: Research on Teaching, Learning and Training

data_deposition.notes: There is an invitation to contribute on the main resource webpage: 'If you notice there is an educational resource, research article or pedagogical tool missing in our database, please consider adding it below in our on submission form or directly into a separate g-forms.'

items.name: Framework for Open and Reproducible Research Training - Replication Database
items.description: FORRT’s Replication Database (FReD) is a community-augmented, quantitative, meta-analytical interface of one of the most comprehensive collections of original and replication findings, including Replications and Reversals and large scale projects such as Many Labs or Registered Replication Reports. Via ReD, students, researchers, and applicants can create summaries of replication findings, search replications, investigate correlates of replicability, and automatically check for replications in reference lists.

items.name: FZ-Juelich B2SHARE
items.description: FZ-Juelich B2SHARE is a service developed by the EUDAT CDI. It provides researchers a solution for storing and sharing small-scale research data from diverse contexts. The local instance at Forschungszentrum Juelich is an offer for everyone within the research centre to share or publish their results with a URL and a PID (persistent identifier). B2SHARE can handle research data in a single file and distributed data across multiple files. The research data and additional metadata are stored in one record. While creating a record the user is able to fill in the (community specific) metadata. Each submitted record and each file within the record is provided with a PID. The PID can be used in publications to refer to the research data. The local B2SHARE instance at Forschungszentrum Juelich assigns DOIs as DataCite repository FZ-Juelich B2SHARE.

data_deposition.notes: institutional members only

items.name: Galoá Proceedings.Science
items.description:
Proceedings.Science is an open access repository and publishing platform managed by Galoá. It is dedicated to hosting, organizing, and preserving conference proceedings, extended abstracts, and academic papers from various scientific events, ensuring they are findable and accessible to the global research community.

Galoá Science is a Crossref Sponsor and a member of the ORCID Consortia, ensuring persistent identifiers and interoperability for all hosted research objects.

data_deposition.notes: Data deposition is restricted to event organizers and authors through the Galoá platform and partner Latin American research institutions.

items.name: Garden
items.description: Garden is a platform for publishing, discovering and running scientific AI models (in areas like materials science, structural biology and astrophysics). It provides each model as a runnable function with metadata, benchmarks and a consistent interface so researchers can quickly test or reuse models without dealing with intricate setup.

items.name: Geochemical Earth Reference Model
items.description: Geochemical Earth Reference Model contains summary data on the geochemistry of all reservoirs in the Earth. All search results are customizable, allowing the user to sort and convert units and to download the data in a format of your choice with one click. This relational database only includes peer-reviewed data.

items.name: Geochemistry of Rocks of the Oceans and Continents
items.description: The Geochemistry of Rocks of the Oceans and Continents (GEOROC) database is a collection of published analyses of igneous rocks and mantle xenoliths. It contains major and trace element concentrations, radiogenic and nonradiogenic isotope ratios as well as analytical ages for whole rocks, glasses, minerals and inclusions. Samples come from 11 different geological settings. Metadata include, among others, geographic location with latitude and longitude, rock class and rock type, alteration grade, analytical method, laboratory, reference materials and references.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Geological and Environmental Reference Materials
items.description: GeoReM is a Max Planck Institute database for reference materials of geological and environmental interest, such as rock powders, synthetic and natural glasses as well as mineral, isotopic, biological, river water and seawater reference materials. GeoReM contains published analytical data and compilation values (major and trace element concentrations and mass fractions, radiogenic and stable isotope ratios). GeoReM contains all important metadata about the analytical values such as uncertainty, analytical method and laboratory. Sample information and references are also included.

items.name: GeologyOntario
items.description: GeologyOntario is an online geoscience information portal maintained by the Government of Ontario that provides access to geological and mineral exploration information for the province. It contains geological maps, reports, assessment files, geophysical data, mineral and mining information, and other geoscience datasets. The platform brings together information compiled from government sources, historical records, and geoscience experts, with data and reports available for viewing and download. It is primarily used for geological research, mineral exploration, mining, and natural resource management.

items.name: Geothermal Data Repository
items.description: The GDR provides free access to data generated from projects funded by the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Geothermal Technologies Office.  It was established to receive, manage, and make available all geothermal-relevant data generated from DOE-funded projects.  Its primary objective is to make high-value data universally accessible and to to protect DOE’s investment in research and development through proper data management and the open transfer of knowledge, to fuel innovation, reduce duplication of effort, and promote scientific discovery in the geothermal sector.

items.name: GHDDI Info Sharing Portal
items.description: GHDDI Info Sharing Portal is the public information sharing portal and data repository for the drug discovery community, initiated by GHDDI. We are making our drug discovery capabilities and resources available at no cost to all researchers who are developing new treatments for COVID-19.

data_deposition.notes: User can share data but after approval and through collaboration with the resource team.

items.name: GitHub
items.description: GitHub Inc. is a Git-based software repository that provides version control. It offers all of the distributed version control and source code management (SCM) functionality of Git as well as adding its own features. It provides access control and several collaboration features such as bug tracking, feature requests, task management, and wikis for each project. It provides a number of different access levels, from free through to paid services.

data_access.notes: GitHub Privacy Statement

data_deposition.notes: GitHub Terms of Service

items.name: GitLab
items.description: GitLab is a Git-based source code repository with wiki and issue tracker functionality. It provides a number of different access levels, from free through to a number of paid services.

data_access.notes: Access is subject to fees

data_deposition.notes: Functionalities are subject to fees

items.name: Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking
items.description: Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking (GNPS) is a web-based mass spectrometry ecosystem that aims to be an open-access knowledge base for community-wide organization and sharing of raw, processed or identified tandem mass (MS/MS) spectrometry data. GNPS aids in identification and discovery throughout the entire life cycle of data; from initial data acquisition and analysis, to post publication exploration. GNPS provides the ability to analyze a data set and to compare it to all publicly available datasets by building on the computational infrastructure of the University of California San Diego (UCSD) Center for Computational Mass Spectrometry (CCMS), and providing public dataset deposition and/or retrieval through the Mass Spectrometry Interactive Virtual Environment (MassIVE) data repository. To provide open and transparent solutions for mass spectrometry (MS) data reuse, data sharing, and analysis reproducibility, the GNPS Dashboard collaborative interactive web application, provides tools to facilitate the exploration of liquid and gas chromatography(LC/GC)–mass spectrometry (MS) data for collaborative examination. The GNPS Dashboard is a hands-on platform for use of private and publicly available MS data, including files stored at long-term MS data repositories such as GNPS/MassIVE, MetaboLights, ProteomeXchange, and the Metabolomics Workbench.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

data_access.notes: CC0 by default for batch upload

data_deposition.notes: free login required

items.name: GlycoNAVI
items.description: GlycoNAVI is a repository of data relevant to carbohydrate research. It contains a free suite of carbohydrate research tools organized by domain, including glycans, proteins, lipids, genes, diseases and samples.

items.name: GlycoPOST
items.description: GlycoPOST is a mass spectrometry data repository for glycomics. Users can release their "raw/processed" data via this site with a unique identifier number for the paper publication. Submission conditions are in accordance with the Minimum Information Required for a Glycomics Experiment (MIRAGE) guidelines.

items.name: GlycoProtDB
items.description: GlycoProtDB is a glycoprotein database providing information of Asn (N)-glycosylated proteins and their glycosylated site(s), which were constructed by employing a bottom-up strategy using actual glycopeptide sequences identified by LC/MS-based glycoproteomic technologies. The database is searchable using gene ID, gene name, and its description (protein name) as query. Each data sheet of glycproteins is based on a single amino acid sequence in Wormpep database for C.elegans and NCBI Refseq database for mouse. The sheet presents actually detected N-glycosylation site(s) which are displayed each capturing methods of glycopeptide subset, e.g., lectins Concanavalin A, wheat germ agglutinin (WGA), or HILIC (hydrophilic interaction chromatography), as well as potential N-glycosylation sites (NX[STC], X≠P). Protein sequences, which have common glycopeptide sequence(s), are linked each other.

items.name: GlyCosmos Glycoscience Portal
items.description: The GlyCosmos Portal is a Web portal aiming to integrate the glycosciences with the life sciences. It consists of Standards, Repositories and Data Resources, providing information about genes, proteins, lipids, pathways and diseases.

items.name: GlyGen: Computational and Informatics Resources for Glycoscience
items.description: GlyGen is a data integration and dissemination project for carbohydrate and glycoconjugate related data. GlyGen retrieves information from multiple international data sources and integrates and harmonizes this data. This web portal allows exploring this data and performing unique searches that cannot be executed in any of the integrated databases alone.

items.name: GlyTouCan
items.description: The international glycan structure repository for glycans published in the literature. Any glycan structure, ranging in resolution from monosaccharide composition to fully defined structures can be registered and have an accession number assigned as long as there are no inconsistencies in the structure.

data_deposition.notes: Free login is required.

items.name: Golm Metabolome Database
items.description: The Golm Metabolome Database (GMD) provides gas chromatography (GC) mass spectrometry (MS) reference spectra, reference metabolite profiles and tools for one of the most widespread routine technologies applied to the large scale screening and discovery of novel metabolic biomarkers.

data_access.notes: Access to the online contents and services of the GMD is granted to all users without any limitations pursuant to the regulations stipulated below.

items.name: Griffith Research Online
items.description: Griffith Research Online is a digital archive of research and scholarship from Griffith University, Brisbane, Australia.

items.name: GRIIDC
items.description: GRIIDC is a multidisciplinary data repository that stores and disseminates data primarily collected or generated from the Gulf of Mexico region. Data can be searched and downloaded for free and data can be stored for a fee. Datasets are assigned digital object identifiers and are described with ISO-19115-2 metadata. Our mission is to ensure a data and information legacy that promotes continual scientific discovery and public awareness of coastal and marine ecosystems.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

data_access.notes: Data are free to download.

data_deposition.notes: Submission only for scientists funded by the Gulf of Mexico Research Initiative, Florida RESTORE Act Centers of Excellence Program, Mississippi Based RESTORE Act Center of Excellence, the National Academies of Sciences Gulf Research Program, the Harte Research Institute for Gulf of Mexico Studies, and others.

items.name: GSA Data Repository
items.description: The GSA Data Repository was established in 1974 as an open archive in which authors of articles in GSA journals and books could place information that supplemented and/or expanded on their article. A unique number was included in a footnote with the printed article (ex: 2007001 is entry 1 for 2007). Hard copies were mailed on request until the Repository went online. In the early 2000s, the remaining hard copies were scanned and posted online as well. In 2020, GSA moved the Repository to Figshare.

items.name: Göttingen Research Online Data
items.description: Göttingen Research Online is an institutional repository for the publication of research data at the Göttingen Campus.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Harvard Dataverse Repository
items.description:
Harvard Dataverse Repository is a research data repository running on the open source Dataverse software. The repository is fully open to the public, allows upload and browsing of data from all fields of research, and is free for all researchers worldwide.

Harvard Dataverse Repository receives support from Harvard University, public and private grants, and an emergent consortium model.

licences.name: Harvard Dataverse General Terms of Use
Harvard Dataverse API Terms of Use
Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

data_access.notes: https://guides.dataverse.org/en/6.7/user/find-use-data.html

data_deposition.notes: User account registration required. Upload limit of 2.5 GB; 1 TB storage space per researcher.

items.name: heiDATA
items.description: heiDATA is Heidelberg University’s research data repository. It is managed by the Competence Centre for Research Data, a joint institution of the University Library and the Computing Centre. All researchers affiliated with Heidelberg University can use this service for archiving and publishing their data. heiDATA runs on software from the Dataverse Project.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

data_access.notes: Open source tool

data_deposition.notes: University of Heidelburg researchers only

items.name: HELLANICUS Institutional Repository - University of the Aegean
items.description:
The Library HELLANICUS Institutional Repository of the University of the Aegean is a service for depositing digital documents which are produced by the Institution’s academic community as a result of its scientific and research activities and which, to a great extent, are not commercially available.

The main aim of the Hellanicus Institutional Repository is to collect, organize, publicize and maintain the scientific work of the members of the academic community in a way that ensures an easy and seamless access to it. Examples of this work include scientific articles - published or not - seminar lectures, textbooks, teaching material, dissertations and PhD theses, multimedia material and videotaped lectures.

items.name: Hellenic Academic Research Data Repository
items.description: HARDMIN (Hellenic Academic Research Data Management Initiative) is Greece’s national repository for research data produced by Greek researchers and academics. It provides secure storage, publication, and long-term access to research data, enhancing transparency, reusability, and digital transformation in the research field.

data_deposition.notes: Only researchers from Greek universities are allowed to upload their datasets.

items.name: HEP Drug Interactions
items.description: Currently 170 million people worldwide are infected with the hepatitis C virus (HCV) and >300 million with hepatitis B (HBV). Although interferon-free combination direct acting antivirals (DAAs) regimens have improved tolerability and efficacy for HCV-infected patients, drug-drug interactions (DDIs) have the potential to cause harm due to liver dysfunction, multiple comorbidities and comedications. This web site was established in 2010 by members of the Department of Pharmacology at the University of Liverpool to offer a resource for healthcare providers, researchers and patients to be able to understand and manage drug-drug interactions.

licences.name: HEP Drug Interactions Terms and Conditions

items.name: High Energy Physics Data Repository
items.description: The Durham High Energy Physics Database (HEPData) has been built up over the past four decades as a unique open-access repository for scattering data from experimental particle physics. It currently comprises the data points from plots and tables related to several thousand publications including those from the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). HEPData is funded by a grant from the UK STFC and is based at the IPPP at Durham University.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: HilReDa
items.description: HilReDa is the University of Hildesheim’s own research data repository. Members of the University of Hildesheim can publish their research results there in the form of research data. This ensures that the data is permanently preserved and made publicly available as open access in a sustainable and high-quality manner.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: HIV Drug Interactions
items.description: Around 37 million individuals are living worldwide with HIV and although advances in therapy have yielded effective regimens, individual antiretroviral drugs are amongst the most therapeutically risky for drug-drug interactions (DDI) presenting significant risks to patients and a challenge for health care providers to ensure safe and appropriate prescribing. In order to address this, the Liverpool Drug Interactions website was established in 1999 by members of the Department of Pharmacology at the University of Liverpool to provide a freely available drug-drug interaction resource.

licences.name: HIV Drug Interactions Terms and Conditions

data_deposition.notes: Only data deposition suggestion is possible.

items.name: HumanCyc
items.description: HumanCyc is a bioinformatics database that describes human metabolic pathways and the human genome. By presenting metabolic pathways as an organizing framework for the human genome, HumanCyc provides the user with an extended dimension for functional analysis of Homo sapiens at the genomic level.

items.name: IdeaExchange@UAkron
items.description: IdeaExchange@UAkron is the institutional repository for The University of Akron in the state of Ohio. A variety of research based documents and media are collected and preserved including working papers, published articles, conference proceedings, student theses, and archival materials. These documents are made available freely whenever possible.

data_deposition.notes: Any professor, faculty, staff, or student at The University of Akron may submit scholarly peer reviewed journal articles, book chapters, dissertations, working papers, or conference proceedings to IdeaExchange.

items.name: IEEE DataPort™
items.description:
IEEE DataPort™ is an online data platform created, owned, and supported by IEEE, a technical professional organization. The web-based platform enables researchers to store, share, access and manage research data.
IEEE DataPort™ provides a DOI for each dataset, supports Open Access/Open Science initiatives, enables dataset owners to retain copyright and ownership rights, supplies data management workflows, and  and provides 2TB/dataset storage capacity for individuals and 10TB/dataset storage capacity for members of institutional subscribers.  All datasets are stored in Amazon AWS S3 to simplify dataset access, analysis and management. Standard datasets may be uploaded for free, and will then be available to DataPort™ subscribers. Data owners can also pay a fee to publish an "Open Access" dataset that is available to all IEEE DataPort™ users without requiring a paid subscription or membership. DataPort™ subscribers can also host private or public data competitions that provide non-subscribers with time-limited access to applicable dataset files.

data_access.notes: only paid submission can be made open access

data_deposition.notes: free submission has multiple constraints

items.name: IIT Dataverse
items.description: IIT Dataverse is the institutional research data repository of the Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia. IIT Dataverse has been operative since May 2021 and is currently open to IIT-affiliated researchers for research data deposition and sharing.

items.name: Illinois Data Bank
items.description: The Illinois Data Bank is a public access repository for publishing research data from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

items.name: IMP: bridging the gap for medicinal plant genomics
items.description: Medicinal plants have garnered significant attention in ethnomedicine and traditional medicine due to their potential antitumor, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. Recent advancements in genome sequencing and synthetic biology have revitalized interest in natural products. Despite the availability of sequenced genomes and transcriptomes of these plants, the absence of publicly accessible gene annotations and tabular formatted gene expression data has hindered their effective utilization. IMP (Integrated Medicinal Plantomics) is a freely accessible platform storing genetic, genome assembly, and transcriptome sequencing data encompassing various organs, tissues, developmental stages and stimulations.

items.name: Imperial College Research Computing Service Data Repository
items.description: A lightweight digital repository for data based on the concepts of collections of filesets and the relationships between them. Both the collection and the fileset are assigned a DOI by the DataCite organisation which can be quoted in articles. Browsing and data deposition are available only when logged in.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

data_access.notes: Data browsing under login

items.name: INCLUDE Data Hub
items.description: The INCLUDE (INvestigation of Co-occurring conditions across the Lifespan to Understand Down syndromE) Project is an NIH-wide collaboration that seeks to improve health and quality-of-life for people with Down syndrome. The INCLUDE Project Data Coordinating Center and partners created the INCLUDE Data Hub, a centralized data resource that allows access to large-scale clinical and multi-omics datasets specific to Down syndrome and supports collaborative, cloud-based analysis to accelerate scientific discoveries related to Down syndrome and its co-occurring conditions.

data_access.notes: Study and Dataset metadata are openly availably through the Public Studies Page (https://portal.includedcc.org/public-studies). Users must create a free Data Hub account and agree to Terms and Conditions to access registered-tier data. Controlled-access data is only available through dbGaP.

data_deposition.notes: Contact info@includedcc.org to share Down syndrome-related data

items.name: India Data Portal
items.description: India Data Portal 2.0 emerges as the country's first research initiative dedicated to public service, offering geo-coded, LGD-mapped, high-spatial time series data from government sources, integrating technological innovation to establish data as a public good.

items.name: Information Platform for Chemical Monitoring
items.description: IPCHEM - the Information Platform for Chemical Monitoring is the reference access point for discovering chemical monitoring data collections which are managed by and are available to European Commission bodies, Member States, international and national organisations and research communities.

items.name: Infoscience - EPFL Institutional Repository
items.description: Infoscience is the institutional repository of EPFL for disseminating scientific publications and research output. It collects, preserves and shares the academic and scientific output of EPFL researchers, teachers and students, making it freely accessible to the largest possible audience.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: INFRA-ART Spectral Library
items.description: The INFRA-ART Spectral Library is a FAIR data service designed as a digital support tool for heritage research specialists working with spectroscopic techniques. With over 3,000 curated spectra, the database allows users to analyze and compare the spectral signatures of a wide range of reference materials, facilitating the identification of 'unknown' samples. The INFRA-ART Spectral Library has been designed, implemented, and optimized over several years, and it currently integrates ATR-FTIR, XRF, Raman, and SWIR reflectance spectra on over 1,400 different materials typically found in works of art.

data_access.notes: Data access policy

data_deposition.notes: Data deposit policy

items.name: Inorganic Crystal Structure Database
items.description: ICSD (Inorganic Crystal Structure Database) was founded in 1977 on the initiative of Prof. Bergerhoff (University of Bonn). Since 1985, FIZ Karlsruhe has been involved in the production of the database with various partners; since 2017, FIZ Karlsruhe has been solely responsible for the product. ICSD is the world’s largest database for fully determined inorganic crystal structures and contains the crystallographic data of published crystalline inorganic structures, including atom coordinates, dating back to 1913. Organometallic and theoretical structures have been added within the past years.
domains: X-ray crystallography 3D molecular structure determination assay

data_access.notes: The user needs to create an account to access the data.

items.name: Institut Laue-Langevin Data Portal
items.description: The Institut Laue-Langevin (ILL) Data Portal is a repository for storage and access to experimental data obtained at the ILL. While individual DOIs for data are accessible, full access to the database, including searching and browsing, requires a login.

data_deposition.notes: Only data from ILL experiments

items.name: Integrated Public Use Microdata Series - International
items.description: IPUMS-International is an effort to inventory, preserve, harmonize, and disseminate census microdata from around the world. The data are coded and documented consistently across countries and over time to facilitate comparative research. IPUMS-International makes these data available to qualified researchers free of charge through a web dissemination system.

items.name: International Ocean Discovery Program Laboratory Information Management System
items.description: The International Ocean Discovery Program (IODP) is an international research collaboration that coordinates seagoing expeditions to study the history of the Earth recorded in sediments and rocks beneath the ocean floor. This resource contains Phase II of the Integrated Ocean Drilling Program and all of the International Ocean Discovery Program data in the new system.

items.name: Internet Archive
items.description: The Internet Archive, a 501(c)(3) non-profit, is building a digital library of Internet sites and other cultural artifacts in digital form. Like a paper library, we provide free access to researchers, historians, scholars, people with print disabilities, and the general public. Our mission is to provide Universal Access to All Knowledge.

items.name: Inxight Drugs
items.description: NCATS Inxight Drugs is a comprehensive and curated portal for translational research. It incorporates and unifies a wealth of data, including manually curated data supplied by the FDA and private companies, and provides marketing and regulatory status, rigorous drug ingredient definitions, biological activity, clinical use, and more. The database offers a substantial amount of manually curated literature data unavailable from other sources.

data_access.notes: All facts appearing in these datasets are in the public domain and may be reproduced or copied without NCATS permission.

items.name: ioChem-BD
items.description: ioChem-BD is a digital repository of Computational Chemistry and Materials results. A set of modules and tools aimed to manage large volumes of quantum chemistry results from a wide variety of broadly used simulation packages.

licences.name: GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL) v3.0 only

items.name: Iowa Research Online - University of Iowa Repository
items.description: Iowa Research Online (ISSN 2476-1680 (online)) preserves and provides access to the research and creative scholarship created by the University of Iowa's faculty, students, and staff. The research papers, theses, dissertations, books, conference presentations, journals, data and multimedia here represent Iowa's rich intellectual and cultural community.

data_deposition.notes: Accepts data deposits from University of Iowa researchers.

items.name: Iowa State University's DataShare
items.description: Iowa State University’s DataShare is an open access repository for sharing, publishing, and archiving research data created by Iowa State University scholars and researchers.

licences.name: ISU Data Share Terms of Use
Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

data_access.notes: Iowa State University’s DataShare is an open access repository.

data_deposition.notes: shares and publishes research data created by Iowa State University scholars and researchers.

items.name: iPPI-DB - Inhibitors of Protein-Protein Interaction Database
items.description: IPPI-DB is a database of modulators of protein-protein interactions. It contains exclusively small molecules and therefore no peptides. The data are retrieved from the literature either peer reviewed scientific articles or world patents. A large variety of data is stored within IPPI-DB: structural, pharmacological, binding and activity profile, pharmacokinetic and cytotoxicity when available, as well as some data about the PPI targets themselves.

data_deposition.notes: Open to everyone who wants to help and maintain the robust manual curation of the database

items.name: ISIS DataGateway
items.description: The ISIS DataGateway is a web-based data repository and discovery portal for the ISIS Neutron and Muon Source (UK) that allows users to browse, explore and visualise experimental data from large-scale science facilities. It supports long-term archival, ingestion and metadata indexing of data to enable better accessibility, reuse and citation of scientific datasets.

items.name: IsoArcH database
items.description: IsoArcH is a non-profit initiative dedicated to preserving and sharing isotopic data for research worldwide.

data_access.notes: Open access

items.name: Minimum Information about a Tailoring Enzyme data repository
items.description: Natural products, also known as specialized or secondary metabolites, are small molecules produced by many organisms. These chemical compounds often show strong biological activities, making them interesting for medicine, agriculture, and other fields. Their biosynthesis is governed by a set of enzymes, which can be separated into gatekeeper/core enzymes, and tailoring enzymes. The latter modify the nascent natural products, giving them their final form, and often confer their biological activity. Tailoring enzymes show a wide range of substrate- and reaction-specificities. The Minimum Information about a Tailoring Enzyme (MITE) data standard was created to facilitate consistent and systematic deposition and retrieval of data on tailoring enzymes. Each MITE entry contains information on a single enzyme: its reaction(s), substrate specificities, known substrate-product pairs, and additional metadata. This record describes the data repository accompanying the data standard.

items.name: ModelSEED Biochemistry Database
items.description: For over 10 years, ModelSEED has been a primary resource for the construction of draft genome-scale metabolic models based on annotated microbial or plant genomes. The ModelSEED biochemistry database is the foundation of the biochemical data underlying ModelSEED and KBase. The The ModelSEED biochemistry database (i) includes compartmentalization, transport reactions, charged molecules and proton balancing on reactions; (ii) is extensible by the user community, with all data stored in GitHub; and (iii) designed as a biochemical ‘Rosetta Stone’ to facilitate comparison and integration of annotations from many different tools and databases. The database was constructed by combining chemical data from many resources, applying standard transformations, identifying redundancies and computing thermodynamic properties. The ModelSEED biochemistry is continually tested using flux balance analysis to ensure the biochemical network is modeling-ready and capable of simulating diverse phenotypes.

The National Repository is a nationwide distributed electronic database in which academic texts are accumulated, stored and systemized. Academic text is a work of a scientific, scientific and technical, educational nature. The purpose of the National Repository is to make the scientific information as accessible to the public as possible for Ukraine and the world, which will contribute to the development of educational, scientific, scientific and technical, innovative activities by improving access to academic texts and promoting academic integrity.

The following types of academic texts in electronic form should be included in the NRAT: dissertations for the scientific degrees and abstracts of dissertations; qualification graduation work of higher education applicants; articles in scientific publications, including all articles (set of articles) on the basis of protection of which the degree has been awarded; monographs, including those for which a scientific degree has been awarded; scientific publications; reports on scientific, scientific and technical activities; deposited scientific works; textbooks, tutorials and other scientific, scientific and teaching materials; publications published by authors on online platforms for the exchange of scientific publications.

The National Repository consists of a central repository maintained by the National Repository Manager, and local repositories maintained by institutional participants.

The National Repository includes all academic texts, regardless of the date of their creation and promulgation in accordance with the established procedure in Regulation.

The National Repository Manager establishes a register of academic texts that is open and contains bibliographic information about academic texts that are included in the central and local repositories, as well as published in electronic or paper forms.

items.name: Open & Sustainable AI Ecosytem
items.description:
Based on the 2025 paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16619), the OSAI AI Ecosystem is a simple interactive, community-maintained digital resource. Its primary function is to serve as a practical registry that supports the implementation of Open and Sustainable AI (OSAI) principles in the life sciences.

The core of the resource is a direct mapping of the paper's OSAI recommendations (for reusability, reproducibility, and environmental sustainability) to a living collection of over 300 real-world components.

These components include a wide array of tools, platforms, standards, and resources that researchers can use to build more sustainable, reusable, and transparent AI. The registry is designed to help researchers "stop searching and start implementing" by allowing them to filter for resources based on their specific goals, such as finding reproducibility tools or sustainability supports.

The resource is supported by an open community-maintained GitHub repository: https://github.com/BioComputingUP/OSAI_ecosystem.

PANGAEA - Data Publisher for Earth & Environmental Sciences  has an almost 30-year history as an open-access library for archiving, publishing, and disseminating georeferenced data from the Earth, environmental, and biodiversity sciences. Originally evolving from a database for sediment cores, it is operated as a joint facility of the Alfred Wegener Institute, Helmholtz Centre for Polar and Marine Research (AWI) and the Center for Marine Environmental Sciences (MARUM) at the University of Bremen. PANGAEA holds a mandate from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)  and is accredited as a World Radiation Monitoring Center (WRMC). It was further accredited as a World Data Center by the International Council for Science (ICS)  in 2001 and has been certified with the Core Trust Seal  since 2019.

items.name: Pergamos: NKUA's Unified Institutional Repository & Digital Library Platform
items.description:
Pergamos is the Unified Institutional Repository & Digital Library Platform of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (NKUA). It has the ability to host any material, whether born digital or digitized, that is either owned and associated with our Institution or produced by the NKUA academic community.  The material hosted by Pergamos, is organised in collections, that, depending on its content, may have an administrator or curator from the staff of respective NKUA units that are related to the collection (who are responsible for the content of the collection they curate). This ensures that compliance with the relevant guidelines or regulations that may govern or affect the content is achieved.
In this respect, Pergamos comprises a large set of heterogeneous digital collections ranging from research and educational output (articles, papers, books, datasets, presentations, etc.) produced by the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens researchers, faculty and staff, to theses and dissertiations produced by NKUA's students, as well as extending to collections of archival, historical or cultural value. More specifically, Pergamos boasts of  more than 10 collections of diverse content, covering almost the entire thematic range of NKUA's Schools, while the total number of digital items reaches approximately 1,000,000 digital objects.
The description of the digital material is based on the Dublin Core metadata standard while the description of the archive material isbased upon the ISAD (G) standard. In each case and depending on the needs of the material, additions have been made to the description of the material either with the Dublin Core (DC qualified schema) specifications or with fields of local use and importance.
Pergamos implements the OAI-PMH (Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting) metadata harvesting protocol, which makes its content searchable by various international websites, harvesters and search engines that support the OAI protocol, in excess of the more or less well known internet search engins (like Google, Bing, etc).
In addition, Pergamos' metadata are compatible with the Europeana Data Model (EDM) standard for platform interoperability with the Europeanana European Digital Library.
Moreover, Pergamos supports an open REST / JSON API for third-party hardware interoperability.

items.name: Practical Journal Insight Project
items.description:

The platform covers tens-of-thousands of journals across all subject areas, uses a highly specific subject classification system, and presents a wide array of different metrics in an interactive and highly customisable interface.
The project supports research by empowering scholars with insights to make informed decisions about where to submit their work. By presenting a variety of novel datapoints - such as journal-reported review times, acceptance rates, editorial board members, word or page limits, and research integrity indicators (and much more)- researchers are better aware of a journal’s standing before they submit. This prevents wasted submission cycles, protects early-career researchers from predatory venues, and aims to incentivise accountability.

items.name: Soybean Knowledge Base
items.description: Soybean Knowledge Base (SoyKB), is a comprehensive all-inclusive web resource developed for soybean translational genomics and molecular breeding. SoyKB stores information about genes/proteins, miRNAs/sRNAs, metabolites, SNPs, plant introduction (PI lines) and traits. It handles the management and integration of soybean genomics and multi-omics data along with gene function annotations, biological pathway and trait information. It has many useful tools including gene family search, multiple gene/metabolite analysis, motif analysis tool, protein 3D structure viewer and data download and upload capacity. It has a user-friendly web interface together with genome browser and pathway viewer, which displays data in an intuitive manner to the soybean researchers, breeders and consumers. The QTLs, SNP, GWAS and traits information is seamlessly integrated in our newly developed suite of tools for the In Silico Breeding Program. It allows integration and extraction of the data in a tabular format as well as graphical visualization in our in-house Chromosome Visualizer. It also supports integration and visualization of Genotype by Sequencing (GBS) data for molecular breeding and phenotypic inferences. In addition, SoyKB now has capacity for incorporation of DNA methylation data and fast neutron mutation datasets. It is also linked seamlessly with P3DB for phosphorylation data. We have also incorporated suite of tools for differential expression analysis for microarray, transcriptomics RNA-seq, proteomics and metabolomics datasets. It includes access to gene lists, Venn diagrams, Volcano plots, functional annotations and pathway analysis. SoyKB is now powered by the iPlant Cyber-Infrastructure. The website is hosted on the iPlant’s advanced computing infrastructure established to leverage the data analysis capabilities.

items.name: Standards for Reporting Enzymology Data Database
items.description: STRENDA DB is a storage and search platform supported by the Beilstein-Institut that incorporates the STRENDA Guidelines in a user-friendly, web-based system. If you are an author who is preparing a manuscript containing functional enzymology data, STRENDA DB provides you the means to ensure that your data sets are complete and valid before you submit them as part of a publication to a journal. Data entered in the STRENDA DB submission form are automatically checked for compliance with the STRENDA Guidelines; users receive warnings informing them when necessary information is missing. A successful formal compliance is confirmed by the awarding of a STRENDA Registry Number (SRN) and documented in a fact sheet (PDF) containing all input data that can be submitted with the manuscript to the journal. In addition, each dataset is assigned a DOI that allows reference and tracking of the data. The data become publicly available in the database only after the corresponding article has been peer-reviewed and published in a journal.

items.name: The Human Metabolome Database
items.description: The Human Metabolome Database (HMDB) is a freely available electronic database containing detailed information about small molecule metabolites found in the human body. The database is designed to contain or link three kinds of data: 1) chemical data, 2) clinical data, and 3) molecular biology/biochemistry data. The database contains 220,945 metabolite entries including both water-soluble and lipid soluble metabolites. Additionally, 8,610 protein sequences (enzymes and transporters) are linked to these metabolite entries. Each MetaboCard entry contains 130 data fields with 2/3 of the information being devoted to chemical/clinical data and the other 1/3 devoted to enzymatic or biochemical data. Many data fields are hyperlinked to other databases (KEGG, PubChem, MetaCyc, ChEBI, PDB, UniProt, and GenBank) and a variety of structure and pathway viewing applets. items.description: University of Warsaw Research Data Repository aims to collect, archive, preserve and make available all types of research data. Storing and making data available is possible for users affiliated with the University of Warsaw, Poland, or those involved in projects carried out in partnership with the University of Warsaw. Browsing and downloading publicly available research data is open to all interested.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: UNM Digital Repository
items.description: UNM’s Digital Repository is an open access institutional repository created to preserve, gather and disseminate scholarship, research and cultural works created by UNM faculty, staff and students within UNM departments, centers and programs. The repository supports teaching and lifelong learning within the UNM campus and broader New Mexico community by making deposited materials permanently and freely accessible.

items.name: Unpaywall
items.description: An open database of free scholarly articles. Unpaywall harvests Open Access content from over 50,000 publishers and repositories, and make it easy to find, track, and use.

data_deposition.notes: Knowledgebase drawn from primary sources, therefore deposition is not applicable.

items.name: UNSWorks
items.description: The UNSWorks (UNSW Open Access Institutional Repository) is the institutional repository of UNSW Sydney (University of New South Wales, Australia), designed to collect, preserve, and disseminate the university’s research outputs. It provides access to a wide range of scholarly materials, including publications, theses, and research datasets, supporting open access and long-term preservation of research outputs. The repository enables UNSW researchers to make their work discoverable and accessible worldwide.

items.name: UPF Digital Repository
items.description: The UPF Digital Repository is the institutional repository of Pompeu Fabra University (Barcelona), designed to collect and disseminate the university’s research output. It includes a wide range of academic materials such as journal articles, working papers, theses, dissertations, and research reports. It also hosts research datasets and supplementary materials supporting publications. The repository is multidisciplinary, covering research produced across all academic fields at the university.

items.name: UQ eSpace
items.description:
The University of Queensland's institutional repository, UQ eSpace, aims to create global visibility and accessibility of UQ’s scholarly research by:

Enhancing discovery of UQ research via search engines such as Google and Trove
Allowing researchers to deposit scholarly works, datasets and open access materials and to view associated metrics
Maintaining a complete and accurate collection of all UQ scholarly works and data sets that feeds into central UQ systems including UQ Researchers and the Academic Portal
Enabling government reporting such as Australian Research Council’s Excellence in Research for Australia and the Engagement and Impact Assessment
Supporting the deposit of open access works to make UQ research globally accessible
Preserving and making digitised materials accessible to the world including HDR theses, photographs, audio materials, videos, manuscripts and other original works.

items.name: USU Institutional Repository
items.description: The Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Repository is the institutional repository of the University of Sumatera Utara (Indonesia), designed to collect, preserve, and disseminate the university’s scholarly outputs. It provides access to academic works such as theses, dissertations, scientific publications, research reports, and other digital documents produced by the university community.

items.name: UVaDOC
items.description: UVaDOC is the institutional digital repository of the University of Valladolid that provides open access to a wide range of academic, scientific, teaching, and institutional documents produced by the university community. It includes full-text resources such as research articles, theses, datasets, educational materials, and historical collections, all freely accessible online.

items.name: UWA Profiles and Research Repository
items.description: The UWA Profiles and Research Repository is an open platform where you can discover University of Western Australia (UWA) staff, find information about their research, teaching, grants, and activities, and access their research outputs.

licences.name: UWA Profiles and Research Repository Copyright and Take-down Requests

data_deposition.notes: Only UWA Staff can deposit data/publication

items.name: UWE Bristol Research Data Repository
items.description: The UWE Bristol Research Repository is an open access online repository providing a central record of the University's research output as well as, whenever possible, immediate access to the full text. It covers the whole range of UWE Bristol's output including books, book chapters, conference papers, images, and journal articles.

items.name: UWinnipeg Borealis
items.description: The UWinnipeg Borealis is the University of Winnipeg’s research data repository hosted on the Canadian Borealis Dataverse platform. It stores and shares finalized research datasets created by University of Winnipeg researchers, making them discoverable and citable online.

items.name: Veterinary Substances DataBase
items.description: Veterinary pharmaceuticals are biologically active and potentially persistent substances which are recognised as a continuing threat to environmental quality. Whilst the environmental risk of agricultural pesticides has had considerable attention in recent decades, risks assessments for veterinary pharmaceuticals have only relatively recently begun to be addressed. Risk assessments and risk modelling tend to be inherently data hungry processes and one of the main obstacles to consistent, accurate and efficient assessments is the need for a reliable, quality and comprehensive data source. The Veterinary Substances DataBase (VSDB) from the Agriculture & Environment Research Unit (AERU) at the University of Hertfordshire provides a comprehensive relational database of physicochemical and toxicological data for these substances.

items.name: VinaR - Repository of the Vinča Institute of Nuclear Sciences
items.description:
VinaR, i.e. Vinča Repository, is a joint digital repository of the all laboratories and departments in Vinča Institute of Nuclear Sciences, University of Belgrade. VinaR provides open access to the publications, as well as to other outputs of the research projects implemented in these institutions.
The software platform (DSpace) meets the current requirements that apply to the dissemination of scholarly publications and it is compatible with relevant international infrastructures.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

data_access.notes: Each repository entry consists of a deposited document and the metadata describing it. Different access and reuse policies apply to metadata and deposited documents. The metadata are freely accessible to all, and freely reusable by all, under the terms of the CC0 license. The deposited content (documents) will be made available to the public, except when forbidden by contracts, rights, or when embargoed for a limited time.  Each deposited item (document) is individually tagged with appropriate license.

data_deposition.notes: In order to deposit content in the repository, you must be affiliated with the Vinča Institute of Nuclear Sciences and have valid credentials. The credentials will be assigned by the repository manager upon registration. All submissions must be approved by a repository manager.

items.name: Virginia Tech Data Repository
items.description: The purpose of the Virginia Tech Data Repository is to highlight, preserve, and provide access to research products (e.g. datasets) of the Virginia Tech community, and in doing so help to disseminate the intellectual output of the university in its land-grant mission. The Virginia Tech Data Repository and Virginia Tech serve the Commonwealth of Virginia, the nation, and the world’s community through the discovery and dissemination of new knowledge.

data_deposition.notes: Only data from Virginia Tech staff.

items.name: WALTZ-DB 2.0
items.description: WALTZ-DB 2.0 is a database for characterizing short peptides for their amyloid fiber-forming capacities. The majority of the data comes from electron microscopy, FTIR and Thioflavin-T experiments done by the Switch lab. Apart from that class of data we also provide the amyloid annotation for several other short peptides found in current scientific research papers. Structural models of the potential amyloid cores are provided for every peptide entry.

items.name: WashU Research Data
items.description: WashU Research Data (Washington University Research Data repository) is a research data repository that allows researchers to share and access datasets across a wide range of disciplines. It contains various types of research data, including textual, tabular, geospatial, imagery, code, and 3D data. The repository supports the long-term preservation, discovery, and reuse of research data.

data_deposition.notes: Students, faculty, and staff of Washington University with an active WUSTL Key can deposit.

items.name: White Rock Open Data Portal
items.description: The City of White Rock Open Data portal offers over 150 structured datasets covering many aspects of city administration and public services. Data types include water treatment results (metals, microbiological indicators), building permits, business licences, city service requests (e.g. streetlight repairs, graffiti removal), and voting records of city council meetings.

items.name: Wikidata
items.description: Wikidata is a free and open knowledge base that can be read and edited by both humans and machines. Wikidata acts as central storage for the structured data of its Wikimedia sister projects including Wikipedia, Wikivoyage, Wiktionary, Wikisource, and others. Wikidata also provides support to many other sites and services beyond just Wikimedia projects. The content of Wikidata is available under a free license, exported using standard formats, and can be interlinked to other open data sets on the linked data web.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: WikiPathways
items.description: WikiPathways is an open, collaborative platform dedicated to the curation of biological pathways. WikiPathways was established to facilitate the contribution and maintenance of pathway information by the biology community.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

data_access.notes: The pathway content at WikiPathways is freely available for download in a variety of data and image formats

items.name: Wolfram Data Repository
items.description: The Wolfram Data Repository is a public resource that hosts an expanding collection of computable datasets, curated and structured to be suitable for immediate use in computation, visualization, analysis and more. Building on the Wolfram Data Framework and the Wolfram Language, the Wolfram Data Repository provides a uniform system for storing data and making it immediately computable and useful. With datasets of many types and from many sources, the Wolfram Data Repository is built to be a global resource for public data and data-backed publication.

items.name: Wolverhampton Intellectual Repository and E-Theses
items.description: Wolverhampton Intellectual Repository and E-Theses (WIRE) is the University of Wolverhampton's open access collection of research outputs produced within the institution, by students, academic or professional staff. All content is openly available, other than valid exemptions for selected embargoed records. Any type of research output authored by a member of the University of Wolverhampton’s research community can be submitted to WIRE, from journal articles, conference contributions and book chapters to exhibitions and digital or visual media.

data_deposition.notes: Submission by students, academic and professional staff only

items.name: WorkflowHub
items.description: The WorkflowHub is a registry of scientific workflows.  WorkflowHub aims to facilitate discovery and re-use of workflows in an accessible and interoperable way. This is achieved through extensive use of open standards and tools, including CWL, RO-Crate, Bioschemas and GA4GH's TRS API, in accordance with the FAIR principles. WorkflowHub supports workflows of any type in its native repository.

data_deposition.notes: Registration required

items.name: World Ocean Atlas
items.description: The World Ocean Atlas (WOA) is a collection of objectively analyzed, quality controlled temperature, salinity, oxygen, phosphate, silicate, and nitrate means based on profile data from the World Ocean Database (WOD). It can be used to create boundary and/or initial conditions for a variety of ocean models, verify numerical simulations of the ocean, and corroborate satellite data.

data_deposition.notes: Submission process is guided by an archive specialist, if the data is selected.

items.name: WueData
items.description: WueData is the institutional research data repository of the Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg (JMU). It enables the publication of research data. The focus of the cross-disciplinary repository is on research data from subjects that do not yet have their own discipline-specific infrastructures for research data management.

data_deposition.notes: The data provider belongs to a chair at the JMU or participates in a project where the JMU is involved in.

items.name: WURM
items.description: The WURM project is a scientific database providing computed physical properties of minerals, including crystal structures, dielectric parameters, and Raman and infrared spectra for a wide range of minerals. These properties are calculated using quantum mechanical methods such as density‑functional theory and presented in an accessible online format.

items.name: WUT Base of Knowledge
items.description: The WUT Base of Knowledge is the Warsaw University of Technology’s institutional research repository. It collects, preserves, and provides access to research outputs, scientific publications, and associated digital materials from the university community.

data_deposition.notes: Content deposit is restricted to authorised academic contributors.

items.name: Wyoming Data Repository
items.description: The Wyoming Data Repository (WDR) supports open discovery and preservation of data outputs produced by University of Wyoming and Wyoming Community College researchers.

items.name: Yabelana
items.description: Yabelana is the institutional research data repository of the University of KwaZulu-Natal (UKZN), South Africa. It enables UKZN researchers to preserve, manage, publish, and share a wide range of research data, including datasets, software, images, videos, and other research outputs. The repository supports long-term preservation, assigns DOIs to datasets, and promotes the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles to improve the visibility and reuse of research data.

data_deposition.notes: UKZN researchers, academic staff, postgraduate students, and other authorized institutional members.

items.name: Yareta
items.description: Yareta is the University of Geneva’s digital research data repository designed to archive, preserve, and share research data over the long term.

items.name: Zenodo
items.description: Zenodo is a generalist research data repository built and developed by OpenAIRE and CERN. It was developed to aid Open Science and is built on open source code. Zenodo helps researchers receive credit by making the research results citable and through OpenAIRE integrates them into existing reporting lines to funding agencies like the European Commission. Citation information is also passed to DataCite and onto the scholarly aggregators. Content is available publicly under any one of 400 open licences (from opendefinition.org and spdx.org). Restricted and Closed content is also supported. Free for researchers below 50 GB/dataset. Content is both online on disk and offline on tape as part of a long-term preservation policy. Zenodo supports managed access (with an access request workflow) as well as embargoing generally and during peer review. The base infrastructure of Zenodo is provided by CERN, a non-profit IGO. Projects are funded through grants.

licences.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

data_access.notes: Files can be flexibly deposited under open, closed, or embargo conditions.

data_deposition.notes: 50 GB per record upload; larger quotas can be requested and granted on a case-by-case basis.

items.name: ZivaHub
items.description: ZivaHub is the institutional open data repository of the University of Cape Town (UCT). It serves as a platform for publishing, preserving, and sharing research data and scholarly outputs produced by UCT students and staff.
